_about: The sights. clickMoa is what one click of elevation moves the strike, windageClickMoa one click of windage, in minutes of angle; clicks is the travel each way from the middle. zoom is the magnification range; fovFtAt100 the field of view in feet at 100 yards at the lowest and highest zoom. frontPostMoa is the front post's width over the sight radius (how wide it looks against the target); apertureMoa the rear ring's lit circle and notchMoa the rear notch's width as the eye sees them; dotMoa a red dot's size. leaf is a sliding rear leaf: its marked settings, the service load it was cut for, and each setting's angle above the 100 m setting, derived with the engine (leaf545: the same leaf on the 5.45x39 rifle, cut for its own load). notchDepthMoa is the rear notch's depth as the eye sees it; stemWidthMoa a bead's stem; a drop reticle's chevronHalfWidthMoa and markHalfWidthMoa are its drawn widths. aimWanderFactor scales the drawn wander of the aim through this sight (1 where absent). frontBead marks a front sight that is a round bead on a stem rather than a flat post.

ar-irons.name: AR-15 iron sights (front post, rear aperture)

source.note: front post elevation on a 16-inch carbine: 1.25 MOA per click on a 20-inch rifle (https://www.ssusa.org/content/everything-you-wanted-to-know-about-ar-15-service-rifle-iron-sights/), more on the carbine's shorter sight radius; compiled tables give 1.875 (https://smith-wessonforum.com/threads/s-w-m-p-15-iron-sight-adjustment-question.615786) and 1.5 to 2.0 (FM 3-22.9 figures at 25 m, https://www.globalsecurity.org/military/library/policy/army/fm/3-22-9/c05.htm); 1.75 is the middle of the band. read from the search engine's indexed text of this page on the date given: this session's network allowed web search but no page fetches

rear windage on a carbine: 0.5 MOA per click on the rifle, 0.62 to 0.75 on the carbine across the same sources; 0.75 used. read from the search engine's indexed text of this page on the date given: this session's network allowed web search but no page fetches

clicks.estimate: the front post has about 12 clicks of useful travel each way from a mid setting; the rear drum far more. Not a maker figure

frontPostMoa.estimate: the A2 front post is 0.07 in wide seen over a sight radius of about 14.75 in on a 16-inch carbine: 0.07 / 14.75 radians = 16 MOA. Dimensions are the common ones, not a BCM figure

apertureMoa.estimate: the large (0.2 in) aperture seen at about 2.5 in from the eye covers about 4.6 degrees (0.2 / 2.5 radians, 275 MOA); the lit circle inside the dark ring is drawn 300 MOA across

low.estimate: the drawn view is 400 MOA (6.7 degrees) across, 35 ft at 100 yards: the aperture's circle with a little dark ring around it

high.estimate: the same: iron sights magnify nothing

aimWanderFactor.estimate: the aim wanders a little more through the AR's small aperture than through other sights (the view is dimmer and the post coarser); 1.3 times the standard wander, a drawing figure, not a measurement

clickMoa.estimate: IWI publishes no click value; a short-radius folding sight, about 1.5 MOA

markHalfWidthMoa.estimate: how far each hold mark reaches either side of the center line, in minutes of angle: short marks a little narrower than the chevron's base; not a maker figure
